title: Perseverance Hall and neighborhood ballrooms
summary: Halls like Perseverance and Jacinto's where he played dances and picnics; he played more jobs than famous names.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Early thirties. And I guess even where before that time, you know. Poison River Hall was blooming then. Remember the old Poison River Hall?
Yeah, very near that hall, the Poison River Hall, all those old halls, things was happening with them then. People give plenty of things they call bonkers.
Well, that's around 1600 Block Virid Street between Sempernard Avenue and then that street.
Uh, yeah. Now, uh, San Jacinto was gone.
Sure, Jacinto's all the more. He'd commonly hall, Jacinto's all that.
How many of them did you work in?

I worked in all of them. I worked Jacinto's Hall, Jacinto's Hall, I worked those places. I mean many times, I played many dances either. I remember one time, me and my little band, I don't say I ain't got a name, but I had a little band that all the people where I come from, like the Sempernard, they had clubs and everything they give, they hired me. And they give them in the Comedy Hall and they give them in the the hall I just called Virid Street there, Perseverance Hall, and they hired me. You know? I formed a band and played those things. Many things I played, many things. I played picnets. I wanted you to give picnets every Sunday and all that, you know? I played all those things. I played much, much music in my life. Why did I get to be a man without any kind of name? That's the truth. I had more connection playing music in the city of New Orleans. I believe in any band, like I'm talking about the club, including like Lewis Contra, all them people, all those kind of people. But somehow they made a man for themselves. But me, I played more music. I think I played more jobs than all those people because I mean, those people played jobs, you understand, like Bourbon Street.
Yeah. But you were working all over town.
That's right. But I played jobs all over the city, neighborhood ballrooms, everywhere I played jobs, you know? Like that.
